newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana signs offshore oil exploration deal.
newsitem.headline: Ghana signs offshore oil exploration deal.

text.p: Ghana has signed a memorandum of understanding with a U.S. and a South Korean company for off-shore oil exploration in the western area of East Cape Three Points where gas was found in the 1970s.
A statement issued on Tuesday identified the companies as Nuevo Energy Co from the United States and Youkong Limited of South Korea.
Ghana's state-run National Petroleum Company signed for the government. Its role depends on oil being found.

Robert Gaston, Nuevo Energy's first vice-president, said he expected exploration and test drilling to start in the first quarter of 1997. The $10 million cost of the operation would be borne by Nuevo Energy, the statement said.
Officials say they expect the full agreement to be approved once Ghana's newly elected parliament has debated the issue.
Ghana's neighbour, Ivory Coast, already produces a small amount of off-shore oil and foreign oil companies have begun exploring for more in deeper off-shore waters.
Both countries are major cocoa producers. Ghana is also rich in gold.
